fatal_errors: Does not identify the AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic HEA or its initial FCC+B2 microstructure.
Does not specify aging near 600°C for embrittlement and 750°C for ductility recovery.
Replaces the observed ordering-induced embrittlement mechanism with an unsupported generic claim that processing refines microstructure and improves ductility.
Omits enhanced L12 ordering, elevated antiphase-boundary energy, planar slip, jagged B2/FCC phase boundaries, and boundary-tip stress concentrations.
Does not define the observed temperature boundaries or correctly predict minimum ductility at 600°C followed by recovery at 750°C.
explanation: The hypothesis recognizes that a high-entropy alloy might display a ductile–brittle–ductile transition under temperature-dependent processing, but it is too generic to reconstruct the target finding. It neither identifies the alloy nor the aging schedule and misses the central, non-monotonic mechanism: maximal L12 ordering and jagged FCC/B2 phase boundaries produce embrittlement at 600°C, whereas reduced ordering and ductile phase-boundary transition zones restore ductility at 750°C. The proposed experiment could screen for a transition through elongation measurements, but it lacks temperature-resolved aging and measurements of ordering, dislocation pile-ups, crack initiation at jagged boundary tips, or impurity segregation needed to discriminate the target mechanism.
